item.title: As Trump Out-Putins Putin, Russia’s Global Influence Erodes
item.summary: The conflict in Iran may give Moscow a short-term boost economically and in Ukraine. But it has also shown the limits of Russia’s partnerships.

item.title: Iran’s Friends Include China and Russia. But Where are They Now?
item.summary: Iran maintains ties with a range of countries, including Turkey, India, Russia and China. Yet in this war, their support is mostly rhetoric.

item.title: For Xi, Trump’s Embrace of War Proves China Needs More Power
item.summary: China is learning lessons from the war in Iran. Chief among them, the United States may pose an even greater threat than Beijing thought.

item.title: Live Updates: New Wave of Airstrikes Batters Tehran
item.summary: The Israeli military said it had sent a broad wave of strikes at the Iranian capital early Saturday. Some strikes hit an area near the Mehrabad Airport. Footage shared on state media showed multiple explosions and columns of smoke.

item.title: Lebanon at ‘Tipping Point’ as It Seeks to Disarm Hezbollah
item.summary: The country is waiting to see if the government seizes on this moment to disarm the Iranian-backed armed group and how the militants will respond.

item.title: Iran’s Drone Attacks Plague the Gulf States
item.summary: Missile launches from Iran have slowed, but relentless drone volleys could deplete air defenses in the region.

item.title: Israel Pushes Farther Into Lebanon, and Readies for More
item.summary: Days into its offensive against Hezbollah, Israel is massing armored vehicles near the Lebanese border for a potentially much larger ground incursion.

item.title: Defense Without U.S. Help Is a Live Topic for Canada, Japan and Australia
item.summary: The leaders of Japan and Canada are making a unified front on defense cooperation as President Trump raises the pressure over military spending.

item.title: ‘Liquor Capital of China’ Is Trying to Save Its Fortunes
item.summary: Once celebrated for its fiery spirits, the town of Maotai has reeled from a bad Chinese economy, changing tastes and a crackdown on boozy official banquets.

item.title: South African President on Trump’s Oval Office ‘Ambush’ and ‘Racist’ Policies
item.summary: In an interview with The New York Times, President Cyril Ramaphosa opened up about the role of middle powers, relations with Washington and apartheid.
